name: HOKM
description: Hokm (meaning 'Command' or 'Order') is Iran's most popular trick-taking card game. A partnership game for 4 players where the Hâkem (Ruler) declares trump after seeing only 5 cards. Teams compete to win 7 tricks per hand and 7 points to win the match. Play proceeds anticlockwise.

content.text: Hokm (meaning 'Command' or 'Order') is Iran's most popular trick-taking card game. A partnership game for 4 players where the Hâkem (Ruler) declares trump after seeing only 5 cards. Teams compete to win 7 tricks per hand and 7 points to win the match. Play proceeds anticlockwise.

Believed to be a descendant of ancient Persian card games, closely related to Court Piece (Coat Piece) played in South Asia. Its current form stabilized with standard French/English decks in the 19th-20th centuries.
4 players in two fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite each other).
Standard 52-card deck. Ranking: Ace (high) down to 2 (low) in all suits.

To determine the first Hâkem, deal cards face-up one at a time anticlockwise until someone receives an Ace — they become Hâkem. For play: the player to Hâkem's right deals. First deal 5 cards to each player. Hâkem looks at 5 cards and declares trump. Then deal remaining 8 cards to each player (13 total).

items.text: Shelem: A bidding variant where players bid on how many tricks they can win. The highest bidder declares trump and must achieve their bid.
Two-Player Hokm: Adapted for 2 players. Each player gets 13 cards. No partnerships.
Rang: A variant where the trump suit is determined by the first card played face-up from the deck, rather than by the Hâkem's choice.
